storyboard.claim: A town is sealed off from the world by an invisible barrier.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Dome, a glass barrier cut over the town, with planes burning against it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the barrier as a physical dome sealing the town, not an abstract wall.

storyboard.claim: People are dying and the air is turning toxic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon while Big Jim sits in his office holding a gold baseball.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The dome is set up; now the cost and the man who benefits.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pairs the deaths with Jim calmly sitting in his office, the gap between the two is the point.

storyboard.claim: With no state police, Jim is smiling at the power he now has.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim smirking in his office; a law icon for the absence of state police.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the deaths to Jim's private satisfaction.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk shows he is pleased, the law icon names what is missing.

storyboard.claim: The real monster is inside the town, not outside the dome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim pointing inward at the town, angry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Jim is the source of the threat; the dome is not.
storyboard.addedInformation: Accusing point with an angry face turns the monster idea into a person.

storyboard.claim: Most readers categorise Under the Dome the moment they see it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia holding the novel up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the monster line to the book being discussed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the book itself as the thing being categorised.

storyboard.claim: This is not a breezy romance or a standard thriller with a twist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia pointing at the viewer, neutral, rejecting the genre label.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the book-as-categorised thread into the expectation the hosts reject.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected genre label.

storyboard.claim: The usual reading of an external threat story is wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie looking out past the town edge, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts reject the external-threat reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected framing; Barbie looks outward to show what the usual reading expects.

storyboard.claim: The barrier is just a plot device, not the real story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Dome barrier drawn over the town, with Julia pointing at it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dismisses the outside-threat reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dome icon is the literal barrier the narrator calls a device.

storyboard.claim: The horror is the town's own social order, not the dome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim angrily pointing at the town around him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the barrier to the town's own cruelty.
storyboard.addedInformation: Accusing point with an angry face places the cruelty in the town's leader.

storyboard.claim: The dome removes the outside consequences that held the town in check.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy, worried, thinking over the empty street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the dome changes the town.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried thinking shows the loss of consequence without a symbol.

storyboard.claim: The contrast between the ordinary and the impossible makes the story work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie walking down Chester's Mill main street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves the listener into the town.
storyboard.addedInformation: Walking on an ordinary street sets the everyday baseline.

storyboard.claim: It is an ordinary autumn Saturday with people doing chores.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree with turning leaves on an ordinary street; Julia walking, mildly content.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ordinary baseline before the event.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tree shows the turning autumn leaves the narrator describes.

storyboard.claim: It is a completely normal weekend.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie, relaxed and content, on an ordinary street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Repeats the normalcy just before the event.
storyboard.addedInformation: Genuine ease, since the calm is the point before the break.

storyboard.claim: A dog and an old woodchuck are bumbling along Route 119 at the town edge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie on the highway edge, surprised by the animals walking along the road.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The abrupt start of the event.
storyboard.addedInformation: Surprise shows the abruptness the narrator names.

callout.text: The Dome cuts through the town

storyboard.claim: Both animals are instantly and cleanly sliced into.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie, afraid, at the edge of Route 119 where the animals were.
storyboard.onScreenText: The Dome cuts through the town
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first death, right after the animals.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fear shows the horror of an instant, invisible cut.

storyboard.claim: A Piper airplane disintegrates against the blue sky and rains fire down on the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon over a sky with a falling plane.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The plane follows the animals.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire icon literally shows fire falling; the plane is named in the narration.

storyboard.claim: Chief of Police Duke Perkins is outside raking his lawn when the surge hits.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A law icon for the police chief on his lawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The event reaches the town's law.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: Duke Perkins has no cast key; the law icon carries the role and andy is a placeholder body.

storyboard.claim: The pacemaker explodes inside his chest from the electromagnetic surge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man collapsed on the street, eyes shut.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The chief is hit by the surge.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the placeholder is andy; the collapse reads as fainted, the callout names the cause.

storyboard.claim: The dome isolates the town physically, then legally and morally.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-bucket sorter for the kinds of isolation.
storyboard.onScreenText: Isolated by land, law and morals
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the mechanism behind the event.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sorter names the three kinds of isolation the narrator lists.

storyboard.claim: The town is severed from federal law, supply chains and oversight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim smirking in the office, sitting in the town he now runs.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the physical isolation to the legal one.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk shows Jim gains from the severance.

storyboard.claim: Removing consequences strips away the thin veneer of civilization.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim, relaxed, in the office; the veneer is named in the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the agencies that are now gone.
storyboard.addedInformation: No symbol for a veneer exists; the callout carries the idea.

storyboard.claim: Without outside law, human nature in a vacuum is not kind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Julia, worried, thinking over the empty town street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The summary of what is left after the agencies are gone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried thinking carries the bleak conclusion.

storyboard.claim: The people who take charge step into the vacuum.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon for one person controlling others, with Jim pointing as he takes charge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From human nature to the people who take charge.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer icon shows one man controlling others, which is the leader's role.

storyboard.claim: Food City is a chaotic mess a few days into the dome.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A food icon for the supermarket, Barbie worried in the aisle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the leaders to the scene of the riot.
storyboard.addedInformation: The food icon literally marks the supermarket.

storyboard.claim: Panicked people fight over canned goods in the supermarket.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Junior fighting with a second man over food.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The riot in the supermarket.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two figures fighting read as an actual scuffle.

storyboard.claim: The acting police chief stands there letting the looting happen and does nothing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A blank-faced man standing still while the riot goes on.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the riot scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: Pete Randolph has no cast key; andy is a placeholder with a blank face, the callout names the inaction.

storyboard.claim: A cruel laugh as an old man is pushed to the floor is crisis opportunism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Junior with a cruel smirk on the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the riot with the cruelty.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the old man and the laugher have no cast keys; junior's sinister smirk stands in for the cruelty.

storyboard.claim: The comforting myth that crises forge heroes is rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie, neutral and thinking, as the myth is rejected.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts reject the heroic myth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected myth; the neutral face avoids an upbeat read.

storyboard.claim: Crises create power vacuums that empower opportunists, and Jim is watching.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim, smirking and calculating in his office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the myth to the real pattern.
storyboard.addedInformation: Calculating smirk shows Jim sees the opportunity.

storyboard.claim: Jim wants the riot and needs it to justify rationing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim, smirking, in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Jim's intent behind the riot.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk reads as wanting the chaos.

storyboard.claim: Jim seizes control of the food supply under a false pretext.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A food icon for the supply, with Jim angry in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From wanting the riot to taking the food.
storyboard.addedInformation: The food icon literally marks the food supply.

storyboard.claim: Let the crisis escalate, let people feel terror, then step in as the savior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim smirking, with Julia afraid beside him as the people who feel the terror.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The step-by-step authoritarian playbook.
storyboard.addedInformation: Julia stands for the frightened public while Jim leads.

storyboard.claim: Citizens surrender their autonomy in exchange for food.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon for the surrendered autonomy, with Andy slumped and worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cost of the food deal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains read as bound and controlled, matching surrendered autonomy.

storyboard.claim: Jim seizes the monopoly on violence, the cornerstone of any dictatorship.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon for violence, with Jim angry in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From food to force.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon reads as organised violence.

storyboard.claim: Jim deputizes teenage thugs from the high school, Carter Thibodeau among them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim pointing at the teenagers he is deputizing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from violence to the people he arms.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pointing to the new deputies shows Jim choosing them.

storyboard.claim: The teenagers get guns, badges and armbands in place of the trained police force, a recipe for disaster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Andy, worried and thinking, reacting to the armed kids.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What Jim hands the teenagers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Worried thinking shows the alarm at arming them, the callout lists the items.

storyboard.claim: In a community where the rules stop applying, notice who takes advantage first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Barbie, worried and thinking, on the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A direct address to the viewer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Thinking expression invites the viewer to consider the vacuum.

storyboard.claim: Big Jim knows the teenagers will not ask constitutional questions or care about due process.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim smirking, knowing his deputies will not object.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why Jim chose these teenagers.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk shows Jim's knowing calculation.

storyboard.claim: The teenagers want power, the thrill, and the ability to bully people who looked down on them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Junior, angry, pointing at people he wants to bully.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Their motives.
storyboard.addedInformation: Accusing point with an angry face reads as a bully's threat.

storyboard.claim: By arming the worst of the hierarchy, Rennie bypasses anyone with a moral compass.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jim smirking in the office, the man bypassing the moral ones.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Jim's strategy: bypass anyone who would object.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk reads as calculated; the callout names who is bypassed.
